xBRIEFInfo.author: overdeck/0.0.0
xBRIEFInfo.description: Plan for PAN-3937: OpenCode conversations stop answering when a Task subagent hits a permission ask; pre-allow at launch and add a stuck-turn watchdog

plan.title: OpenCode conversations stop answering when a Task subagent hits a permission ask; pre-allow at launch and add a stuck-turn watchdog
plan.author: agent:claude-fable-5-1

narratives.Problem: OpenCode 1.18.31's ACP permission relay (packages/opencode/src/acp/permission.ts Handler.process()) silently drops permission asks whose sessionID belongs to a Task subagent session (mode=subagent is never registered with ACPSession, so tryGet() misses and the handler returns without ever replying). Overdeck launches `opencode acp` with opencode's stock permission defaults, three of which default to "ask" (external_directory, doom_loop, read for .env globs) and subagents inherit the parent session's external_directory ruleset verbatim (deriveSubagentSessionPermission). When a subagent hits one of these asks, its Deferred never resolves, the parent's task tool call hangs, the parent's session/prompt RPC never resolves, and AcpHost.promptQueue (src/lib/acp/host.ts) never advances — every subsequent operator message queues behind the dead turn forever with no error surfaced. Confirmed live in conv 2834 (2026-09-19): an external_directory /tmp/* ask from a Task subagent produced no permission_request transcript entry and stalled the conversation for 20+ minutes until manually unstuck via the opencode HTTP API's /permission endpoints.
narratives.Proposal: (1) Pre-allow the three ask-by-default permission keys (external_directory, doom_loop, read for .env globs) at launch via the OPENCODE_PERMISSION env var, live-verified to merge correctly into opencode's config and win over its hardcoded defaults. (2) Give the ACP host a deterministic, host-reserved port for the opencode HTTP server it already spawns, and add a host-side watchdog that polls GET /permission and auto-replies {"reply":"always"} to anything pending once a prompt has been stalled past a threshold, logging a permission_outcome transcript entry with source "watchdog" as a visible fallback. (3) Extend the dashboard's existing ACP transcript-derived activity summary with a stalledSince signal and render a muted stuck-turn label in the conversation list. (4) Document the policy, the watchdog, and a generalized manual unstick recipe in configuration/harnesses.mdx and pan-diagnose.
narratives.NonGoals:
- Filing the upstream anomalyco/opencode bug report is not part of this xBRIEF; left to the operator per the issue text.
- The stalled-turn label ships only in ConversationRow (conversation list), not in the full ConversationPanel header.
- Pre-allowing question, plan_enter, or plan_exit is out of scope — those default to "deny", not "ask", and do not cause this deadlock.
- Changing the ACP relay's own auto-approve policy (selectAutoPermissionOutcome) for primary-session asks is out of scope — that path already works correctly.
- Reworking opencode's own vendored port-selection code (startWithPortFallback) is out of scope — Overdeck works around the gap from the host side instead.

autoDecisions.summary: Pre-allow exactly external_directory, doom_loop, and read (*.env, *.env.*) via OPENCODE_PERMISSION; leave question/plan_enter/plan_exit untouched.
autoDecisions.rationale: Source-verified (packages/opencode/src/agent/agent.ts) that these three keys are opencode's only ask-by-default permissions; question/plan_enter/plan_exit default to deny, which fails fast rather than deadlocking, so widening the pre-allow set to them has no deadlock-prevention benefit.

autoDecisions.summary: Reserve the opencode HTTP server port deterministically from the host (net.createServer().listen(0), close, pass as an explicit --port) instead of discovering it via ss -ltnp against the child PID as the issue text suggested.
autoDecisions.rationale: Live-verified opencode acp --help exposes --port/--hostname flags that win over user config; deterministic reservation avoids brittle process/PID port-scraping and gives both the spawn path and the watchdog the same known value up front.

autoDecisions.summary: Watchdog always replies {"reply":"always"} rather than reusing selectAutoPermissionOutcome.
autoDecisions.rationale: selectAutoPermissionOutcome categorizes ACP's named options list, but the opencode HTTP GET /permission response is a bare PermissionV1.Request with no options list to categorize against — "always" is the only reply shape available and matches Overdeck's existing stance of auto-approving every relayed ask.

autoDecisions.summary: Dashboard stall-banner threshold (300s) set strictly looser than the host watchdog's own trigger threshold (180s) plus one poll cycle.
autoDecisions.rationale: Keeps the operator-facing banner a fallback signal shown only after the host's own automatic recovery has had a full cycle to fire, avoiding a row that simultaneously shows "working" and "stalled" as contradictory states.

autoDecisions.summary: No xBRIEF item files the upstream opencode bug report.
autoDecisions.rationale: Issue text explicitly frames upstream filing as the operator's call; the PRD's Problem section is written so its root-cause paragraph can be pasted directly into that report if the operator chooses to file it.

items.title: Pre-allow OpenCode's ask-by-default permission keys at launch

expected_outputs: opencode.test.ts passes with the updated exact-equality spawn-input assertion including OPENCODE_PERMISSION

narrative.Action: In buildOpenCodeAcpSpawnInput (src/lib/acp/opencode.ts:22-33), always set OPENCODE_PERMISSION in the returned env to the JSON string {"external_directory":"allow","doom_loop":"allow","read":{"*.env":"allow","*.env.*":"allow"}}, merged with any caller-supplied environment. Update the existing opencode.test.ts spawn-input assertion to expect the new env key.

items.title: Given any call to buildOpenCodeAcpSpawnInput for opencode/opencode-go, it returns env.OPENCODE_PERMISSION equal to the exact JSON string {"external_directory":"allow","doom_loop":"allow","read":{"*.env":"allow","*.env.*":"allow"}}
The updated opencode.test.ts exact-equality assertion for buildOpenCodeAcpSpawnInput's return value passes under npx vitest run
Given caller-supplied environment entries such as OPENCODE_API_KEY, buildOpenCodeAcpSpawnInput's returned env object preserves them unchanged alongside the injected OPENCODE_PERMISSION key
Reserve a deterministic port for the opencode HTTP server at host launch

expected_outputs: opencode.test.ts and host.test.ts pass including the new port-argument and kimi-unaffected cases

narrative.Action: buildOpenCodeAcpSpawnInput gains a required port argument and appends ["--hostname","127.0.0.1","--port",String(port)] to args for opencode/opencode-go only. AcpHost.main() reserves a free TCP port (net.createServer().listen(0), read the assigned port, close) before constructing the opencode runtime, threads that port into the spawn-input builder, and passes it into a new optional AcpHostOptions.openCodePort field so AcpHost stores it for the watchdog (item acp-host-permission-watchdog) to read. Kimi's buildKimiAcpSpawnInput and spawn path are untouched.

items.title: Given a port argument, buildOpenCodeAcpSpawnInput appends exactly ["--hostname","127.0.0.1","--port","<port>"] to the returned args array
Given provider opencode or opencode-go, AcpHost.main() reserves a free TCP port before spawning and returns a constructed AcpHost instance whose openCodePort matches that reserved port
Given provider kimi, buildKimiAcpSpawnInput's args contains no --port or --hostname entries and AcpHost.main() skips port reservation
Add a host-side watchdog that auto-replies to permission asks the ACP relay never received

expected_outputs: host.test.ts passes including fake-timer-driven watchdog cases (trigger, no-trigger-before-threshold, kimi-excluded, benign-404)
metadata.readinessReason: Depends only on acp-host-deterministic-port's port value (declared via the blocks edge); once that lands, the watchdog's own files (host.ts, transcript.ts) are touched by no other item and can proceed in its own slot.

narrative.Action: Extend AcpTranscriptEntry.source (src/lib/acp/transcript.ts) to include "watchdog". In AcpHost, for provider opencode/opencode-go only, run a 60s-cadence interval while a prompt is in flight; once 180s have passed with no runtime event observed, GET http://127.0.0.1:{openCodePort}/permission, POST {"reply":"always"} to /permission/{id}/reply for each entry returned, and append one permission_outcome transcript entry per reply with source "watchdog" and the entry's own sessionID. A reply that 404s (already resolved by the relay) is treated as benign, not an error. The interval stops when the prompt operation settles.

items.title: Given a prompt in flight for an opencode-provider host with no runtime event observed for 180 simulated seconds (vi.useFakeTimers), the host issues a GET request to the reserved port's /permission endpoint

Given that GET returns one pending entry, the host POSTs {"reply":"always"} to /permission/{id}/reply and appends a transcript entry with source "watchdog" and content type permission_outcome carrying that entry's sessionID
Given the prompt has been in flight for fewer than 180 simulated seconds since the last runtime event, zero HTTP requests reach the opencode server
Given provider is kimi, the watchdog interval never starts and zero HTTP requests occur regardless of prompt duration
Given a POST /permission/{id}/reply stub returns HTTP 404, the host does not throw and does not append an error-tagged transcript entry for that reply
Derive a stalledSince signal from ACP transcript recency

expected_outputs: activity-summary-acp.test.ts passes including the new stalledSince cases

narrative.Action: Add stalledSince?: string to ConversationActivitySummary. In summarizeConversationActivity's ACP branch, add STALLED_TURN_MS = 300_000 and set stalledSince to the transcript's mtime (ISO string) when isWorking is true and the transcript has not been modified in over 300000ms; otherwise leave it undefined. Thread stalledSince through conversation-list.ts's enriched conversation row alongside the existing isWorking/currentTool fields.

items.title: Given an ACP transcript with an open turn (no turn_completed/prompt_failed since the last prompt) whose file mtime is older than 300000ms, summarizeConversationActivity returns stalledSince set to that mtime as an ISO string
Given the same open-turn transcript but written within the last 300000ms, summarizeConversationActivity returns stalledSince as undefined
Given a transcript whose last event is turn_completed regardless of file age, summarizeConversationActivity returns stalledSince as undefined
Given a conversation whose session file produced a stalledSince value from summarizeConversationActivity, conversation-list.ts's enriched row returns that same stalledSince value unchanged
Render a stuck-turn label in the conversation list row

expected_outputs: ConversationRow.test.tsx passes including the new stalled-label case

narrative.Action: Add stalledSince?: string | null to the Conversation interface in ConversationList.tsx. In ConversationRow.tsx, when conv.stalledSince is set, render a muted text label "waiting on agent — no activity since {HH:MM}" in place of the WorkingSpinner/status dot for that row, following pan-style-guide (muted status text, no decorative color) and the AwaitingInputIndicator aria-label pattern.

items.title: Given a conversation row prop with stalledSince set to an ISO timestamp, ConversationRow renders a muted text label containing "waiting on agent" and the HH:MM formatted from that timestamp
Given stalledSince is unset or null, ConversationRow renders the existing WorkingSpinner/status-dot behavior with no visible change from current output
Given stalledSince is set, ConversationRow renders a stalled label whose aria-label contains the conversation name, matching the existing AwaitingInputIndicator pattern
Document the OpenCode permission policy, watchdog, and unstick recipe

expected_outputs: the exact OPENCODE_PERMISSION JSON and the three pre-allowed keys appear in the OpenCode section
the watchdog's port-discovery, cadence, threshold, and reply policy plus a generalized manual unstick recipe appear in the same section

narrative.Action: In the existing "OpenCode with Go and Zen" section of configuration/harnesses.mdx, add a subsection documenting: the exact OPENCODE_PERMISSION JSON Overdeck sets and why; the deny-override caveat for those three keys; the watchdog's port-discovery mechanism, 60s poll cadence, 180s trigger threshold, and always-reply-"always" policy; and a manual unstick recipe generalized to use the discovered (not hardcoded) port.

The same section contains a statement that this setting overrides a matching user-configured deny for those three keys only, and that all other permission keys are unaffected
The same section contains the watchdog's poll cadence of 60s, trigger threshold of 180s, reply policy of always, and a manual unstick recipe using a discovered port
